title: Proof-of-custody for quota/rate events and tamper-evident audit pipeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Produce an operationally verifiable, tamper-evident chain-of-custody for all events that affect billing (usage tokens consumed, quota checks, rate-limit responses, and manual quota adjustments). This ticket covers the design and prototype of an end-to-end pipeline that signs events at ingestion, stores append-only snapshots with strong retention controls, and exposes reproducible proofs for auditors and disputes. Motivation: customers and compliance teams require demonstrable evidence that billing inputs are immutable and traceable, and that any quota adjustments or rate-limit overrides are recorded with human and system context.
acceptance_criteria: Signed event envelope: every usage/rate/quota event emitted by front-end proxies and internal meterers contains a stable event id, timestamp, upstream request id, and an HMAC or asymmetric signature created with a KMS-backed key.
Append-only storage: events are persisted to an append-only store (S3 with Object Lock in Governance mode + versioning) with lifecycle rules matching retention policy and WORM guarantees.
Daily ledger snapshots: a daily Merkle-root snapshot is produced from ordered events and stored in a separate immutable ticker file for quick tamper detection.
Audit API: read-only audit endpoints allow auditors to request event ranges and receive signed bundles plus a verification recipe; access to these endpoints is RBAC-protected and logged to SIEM.
Reconciliation job: nightly reconciliation between billed tokens and event ledger runs with automated drift alerts and a human review workflow for discrepancies >0.5%.
Access controls & monitoring: only designated SRE and Billing reviewers can export raw event bundles; exports generate high-fidelity audit entries and require approval for PII-containing payloads.
Proof generation: given a range (start_ts, end_ts) the system can output a verifiable proof (signed Merkle path + snapshot) that an event was included or absent.
Performance: signing and persistence path adds <5ms p50 to request tail latency for the metering pipeline or is offloaded asynchronously with equivalent reliability guarantees.
tasks: Design cryptographic envelope format (v1) for meter events and document in Confluence
Implement a lightweight signer library (Go/Python) using KMS-backed keys and HMAC fallback
Modify metering proxies to attach signature and stable event id before publish
Build append-only writer to S3 with Object Lock + partitioning scheme and retention tags
Merkle snapshot generator and signer: daily job to compute root and publish a signed snapshot file
Audit API: read-only service with RBAC and CSV/JSON bundle export endpoints
Nightly reconciliation job and dashboard; alert rules and runbook
E2E tests: tamper detection simulation, signature verification, and permission checks
Run security review and tabletop with Compliance and Legal teams
implementation_notes: We evaluated three approaches: 1) centralized ledger service, 2) append-only object store with signed events, and 3) blockchain-style anchored proofs. Given operational constraints and latency, we selected option 2 as the initial rollout: sign at ingestion using a KMS key (asymmetric) and persist events to S3 with Object Lock. Use a deterministic ordering key (ingest time + monotonically increasing counter per partition) to compute Merkle trees. For scale, partition by customer_id mod 1024 and run parallel snapshot workers. Use SNS -> Lambda (or lightweight worker pool) to batch events for snapshots. Key rotation: new keys sign future snapshots; maintain verification chain by publishing public key material and rotation metadata to the signer registry. For dispute handling, support event-level replays that include original signature and ingestion metadata.
